26a. παιδὶ ἑῷ: to her son, Eros. Lg (P)

b. παιδὶ ἑῷ εἰπεῖν: Apollonius makes Eros the son of Aphrodite, but Sappho (fg inc. lib. 82 Lobel = 132 B. III 131) makes him the son of Earth and Heaven, Simonides (fg 43 B. III 408) the son of Aphrodite and Ares: 'wretched child, guileful son of Aphrodite, whom she bore to Ares the †guileful† contriver.' Ibycus (fg 31 B. III 247) 〈makes him the son of Aphrodite and Hephaestus〉, and Hesiod (Theog. 116 sqq.) says Eros is from Chaos, but in the poems attributed to Orpheus he is the son of Chronos (fg 37 Kern): 'but Chronos begot Eros and all the winds.'
